paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption: Inter-annotator agreement compared to sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and sample-level maximum ambiguity values.
model_annotation: The figure contains two vertical bar charts, each illustrating the relationship between different measures of ambiguity and inter-annotator agreement, as measured by Fleiss Kappa. Both charts have a vertical axis labeled "Fleiss Kappa" with a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 0.8, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. The left chart has a horizontal axis labeled "Ambiguity Std" with values ranging from 0.0 to 0.94, while the right chart has a horizontal axis labeled "Max Ambiguity" with values 1, 2, and 3. The bars in both charts are colored in different shades of blue, with the left chart having values of 0.88, 0.46, 0.03, and 0.24 corresponding to ambiguity standard deviations of 0.0, 0.47, 0.82, and 0.94, and the right chart having values of 0.89, 0.46, and 0.23 corresponding to maximum ambiguity values of 1, 2, and 3, respectively. The bars in both charts are not grouped or stacked, and are presented in ascending order of ambiguity on the horizontal axis, with the left chart showing a decrease in Fleiss Kappa as ambiguity standard deviation increases, except for the last bar, and the right chart showing a decrease in Fleiss Kappa as maximum ambiguity increases. No bars are visually emphasized in either chart.
